Rasters on planes

Source: R/layers-texture.R
geom_raster_3d.Rd

Draws values on a regular grid as one image lying on a plane of the panel, like ggplot2::geom_raster(): each cell is one pixel of a texture (see texture_3d()), so a raster of any size is a single face of the scene. The two positions of plane locate the cells; the remaining axis takes at, or the mapped position on it, and every distinct position on that axis gives its own image, such as one slice of a volume per level.

Usage

geom_raster_3d(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  stat = StatRaster3D,
  position = "identity",
  ...,
  plane = "xy",
  at = NULL,
  interpolate = FALSE,
  hjust = 0.5,
  vjust = 0.5,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, stat, position, ..., na.rm, show.legend, inherit.aes

Standard ggplot2 layer arguments.

plane

Two distinct axis letters: the axes of the cell positions, such as "xy", "xz" or "yz".

at

Position on the remaining axis, overriding a mapped one; NULL uses the mapped position, or the lower box side when it is not mapped.

interpolate

Whether to interpolate between cells. The default shows them as sharp squares.

hjust, vjust

Position of each cell's centre within the cell, as in ggplot2::geom_raster().

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

See also

annotation_raster_3d() for an image, facet_slices_3d().

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = 1:30, y = 1:20)
d$value <- with(d, sin(x / 4) * cos(y / 3))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster_3d() +
  coord_3d()
slices <- expand.grid(x = 1:25, y = 1:25, z = c(1, 2, 3))
slices$value <- with(slices, exp(-((x - 13)^2 + (y - 13)^2) / (20 * z)))
ggplot2::ggplot(slices, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster_3d(alpha = 0.8) +
  coord_3d()
